question.text: Under Section 11 of the Income Tax Act, what proportion of income must a registered charitable trust apply toward its charitable objects in the same year (subject to accumulation rules) to retain full tax exemption?

answer.text: At least 67% — mirroring SEBI ICDR Reg 292B
At least 75% — mirroring Sec 8 Co licence condition
At least 100% — no accumulation is permitted
At least 85% — with up to 15% permitted to be accumulated

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 11(1) permits a charitable trust to retain up to 15% of income and requires application of at least 85% toward its stated charitable objects within the same financial year. Accumulation beyond 15% is permitted only with Form 10 filed under Section 11(2), for up to 5 years and a specific purpose. The Trap: 67% is the SEBI ICDR SE-eligibility threshold — regulatory, not taxation. 75% is not a statutory figure here. 100% is overly strict. Cross-Exam Context: V-A / X-A (MF Distributor / IA) cover donor-side 80G; XXIII tests SE-side Section 11 application. The 85% is SE-side recurring compliance. Assessor's Pro-Tip: Build an '85% application' reconciliation into your SAS-100 limited-assurance workpaper: match Receipts → Qualifying Application (programme spend + capex on charitable asset + specified deposits). If the ratio falls below 85% and no Form 10 filed, the income becomes taxable at 30% — which kills donor confidence.
